turns.narration:
You stop one step before the meditation circle and let the latecomer’s place stay empty beside you. Kira is not here. That is the first thing the temple gives you this morning, and Luke keeps walking without glancing at the gap. Bare feet whisper over stone worn smooth by thousands of years of prayer, and the sound makes the silence feel supervised.

The upper level is all pale dust and old heat. The Great Temple’s inner wall rises beside you, cut from black stone that does not belong on Yavin 4. It drinks the light instead of reflecting it. A narrow seam runs through one block at shoulder height, filled with something green and hard that looks like sap until you stare long enough to know it is not.

You fold yourself into the nearest open space and lower your gaze. Twelve students breathe in uneven rhythm. Luke passes behind them, slow enough that nobody has to pretend not to notice him. His presence brushes the edge of your awareness, steady and clear. Not an order. Not a warning. A hand held out and waiting.

Below, a generator coughs, catches, and drops back into its grind. The old temple answers with a faint tremor through the floor. You feel that through your knees before you hear it in the walls. Useful. Fragile. Still standing.

Kira’s absence sits at the edge of your focus like a chipped bead rolling in your palm. You know her well enough now to hear the difference between lateness and avoidance. This feels like the second one. You keep your face still and your hands on your thighs. There are places in the jungle where a person can hide from a teacher. There are fewer places where they can hide from the Force, and even fewer where they can hide from someone who already knows to look.

Luke stops near the center of the circle. He does not speak right away. He looks across the students, then toward the far archway that opens to the jungle, where humidity glows green beyond the stone. When he finally speaks, his voice stays low.

“Hold the breath. Let it go.”

You do. The air tastes faintly of wet moss and old stone. Beneath that, there is another scent, thin as a cracked wire insulation: ozone from the generator, carried up through the temple’s throat.

Kira is still late. The Massassi stone is still older than anything built around it. And somewhere below your feet, something in the lower levels is waiting in silence that does not belong to morning.

You sit straighter. You can feel the day narrowing around that missing space.
choices: Watch the temple mouth and keep one part of your mind on Kira’s absence; if she comes in now, you want to see her face before she sees yours.
Slip out after the meditation cue and head for the lower Massassi levels, following the generator’s cough before it changes again.
Ask Luke, plainly and in front of everyone, where Kira is; if he evades, his answer will tell you something.
Turn the blank Mirialan bead between your fingers and sit with the empty space beside you, letting the silence tell you what you already know.

turns.action: Ask Luke, plainly and in front of everyone, where Kira is; if he evades, his answer will tell you something.
turns.narration:
You ask it in front of everyone, plain as a blade laid on a table.

Luke’s eyes lift from the floor seal at the center of the circle. He does not turn his head right away. When he does, his gaze lands on you first, then passes once over the empty space where Kira should be.

“Not here,” he says.

A couple of the other students keep their hands folded and their faces down. One of them blinks too hard and stares at the Massassi stone. Luke sees that too. He always sees more than he says.

He gets to his feet in one smooth motion and rests both hands on his belt, calm enough to make the room feel smaller. “She left before dawn.”

Before dawn. Not late. Not forgotten. You feel the difference in your ribs.

Luke’s mouth tightens, then eases. “If you’re asking whether I sent her somewhere, I didn’t.”

That answer is careful. Not evasive. Not complete either.

The generator hum crawls up through the floor seam behind you, thin and steady. Luke glances toward the high windows that look out into the jungle, then back to you. “She’s been carrying something around since yesterday. I told her to get sleep. She said she would.”

He pauses just long enough to make the next part matter. “She went toward the lower corridors.”

The words land hard against the old stone. Lower corridors. Not the jungle. Not her quarters. Not the mess.

You know the shape of the lie now, or the beginning of it. Somebody has been moving where the temple keeps its buried things.

Luke studies your face without moving closer. “If you know more than I do, say it.”

There it is. No edge. No threat. Just an open door with a hallway behind it.

Your prayer beads press cold against your wrist.
choices: Tell Luke you’ve seen Kira’s pattern of evasion and keep your voice even; ask for access to the lower Massassi levels before the day gets crowded
Say only that Kira is hiding something and you need the truth before it reaches the wrong hands; let Luke decide how much he wants to share
Keep the question on the temple itself and ask Luke what waits beneath the Great Temple that would draw her downstairs in the dark
Hold the answer back for now, and sit with the empty space beside you long enough to decide whether trust means speaking first or waiting longer

turns.action: Tell Luke you’ve seen Kira’s pattern of evasion and keep your voice even; ask for access to the lower Massassi levels before the day gets crowded
turns.narration:
You keep your voice even and ask for the lower Massassi levels before the day gets crowded. Luke does not answer right away. He looks past you, to the circle, to the empty space where Kira should be, then back to you with the same calm he uses when a practice remotes starts spitting sparks.

“Not alone,” he says.

That is not a refusal. It is a boundary.

He pushes up from the stone and motions once with two fingers for you to follow. The other students keep their eyes forward. Tionne’s gaze tracks the two of you for a beat, then returns to the old markings in the floor. Luke leads you past the meditation circle and into a corridor where the temple stones run cold under your sleeve. The air changes after ten paces. Temple dust gives way to something older and wetter, with a trace of machine coolant from the maintenance lines buried in the walls.

At the sealed stair, Luke pauses. The door is still set into the Massassi stone, its edges worn smooth by time and use. A narrow panel sits beside it, newer than the temple by millennia.

“Jungle starts chewing at these stairs after sunset,” he says. “Try not to make me regret this before lunch.”

He keys the panel. The seal hisses. A draft rolls up from below carrying damp stone and rust.

For a moment, you catch it again — not sight, not sound. A pressure in the Force from below the temple, dark and still as deep water. It does not lunge. It waits.

Luke watches you catch it.

“Tell me what you’re feeling,” he says quietly, “and leave out the part where you pretend you’re fine.”

Your prayer beads are still cold against your wrist.
choices: Tell him the lower levels feel wrong in a way the jungle never does, and ask whether Kira has been going there on her own
Step to the sealed stair and insist on going first; if the temple wants to bite, let it bite you before it reaches anyone else
Keep your face level and ask Luke who else knows about the lower Massassi levels, because this stops being about Kira the moment someone starts lying
Shut your mouth for once and listen to what the dark-side vergence beneath the temple is saying before you decide whether to go down

turns.action: Keep your face level and ask Luke who else knows about the lower Massassi levels, because this stops being about Kira the moment someone starts lying
turns.narration:
Luke doesn’t give you the answer you asked for. He gives you the shape of the room around it.

His hand stays on the panel a beat too long before he pulls it away. He looks past you toward the rest of the circle, where the others have gone quiet enough to pretend they are not listening.

“Not many,” he says. “Tionne. Me. A few people who move supplies. No one else needs to know.”

He keeps his voice level. The words do not.

The seal below stays open, breathing damp stone into the morning. The dark-side vergence beneath the Great Temple sits under that breath like a blade laid flat in a drawer.

You meet his eyes and keep your own face still. “That’s the problem,” you say. “The moment someone starts lying, it stops being about Kira.”

Luke’s mouth tightens once. He glances down at your prayer beads, then back up. “That’s a fair complaint.”

It is not an admission. It is close enough to matter.

A soft scrape sounds from the edge of the meditation circle. Tionne has not left. She stands with her hands folded in her sleeves, her gaze fixed on the open seal rather than on either of you. “If you want the truth about the lower Massassi levels,” she says, “I can give it to you. What I cannot give you is a simple reason Luke kept it quiet.”

Luke exhales through his nose. “That sounded like criticism.”

“It was meant as a note,” Tionne says, and there is the faintest trace of dry amusement in it. “The lower levels were not built for curiosity. The old Jedi left warnings there for a reason. The Massassi used these stones for blood rites long before Luke’s students started walking them in clean boots.”

That lands harder than any lecture. The humid air from below feels colder against your wrists.

Luke shifts his weight. “That’s exactly why I wanted time before everyone knew.”

“And Kira?” you ask.

His eyes flick once, toward the far side of the temple where she should have been this morning. “Kira is already too interested. I was trying to keep that from becoming everybody’s problem at once.”

Tionne looks at him then, not unkindly. “You hear that sentence often enough, Luke, and it starts to sound like wisdom.”

He gives her a tired, almost embarrassed look. “I’m collecting those.”

You let the silence sit for half a breath. The open seal below hums with trapped moisture and old stone. “Who else knows?” you ask again, quieter this time. “Not who should. Who does.”

Luke’s answer comes after a pause that shows its own shape. “Kira knows enough to be dangerous to herself. You know enough to be angry with me. Tionne knows the history. And there are details I have not shared with the students because I did not want fear doing my teaching for me.”

That one lands where it is meant to. He is not dodging now. He is choosing the shape of the truth.

Tionne steps closer to the seal and folds one hand over the other. “If you go below, go because you want to understand, not because you want to prove someone wrong. The temple will punish vanity before it punishes fear.”

Luke looks at you again, direct and plain. “I should have told you more.”
choices: Hold his gaze and tell him that hiding things to keep people safe is how people get hurt anyway; ask for the full history of the lower Massassi levels, now, before anyone else goes below.
Tell Tionne you want the history from the beginning, with no omissions, and ask her to show you what the old warnings actually say
Ask Luke to call Kira back up here and put the truth in front of her before she goes looking for it alone
Say nothing. Let the apology stand, and decide whether you can live with Luke’s version of trust before you give him yours.

turns.action: Ask Luke to call Kira back up here and put the truth in front of her before she goes looking for it alone
turns.narration:
You ask Luke to call Kira back up here and put the truth in front of her before she goes looking for it alone.

Luke holds your gaze for a beat, then gives a small nod and reaches for the comm panel by the seal. “Kira. Meditation level. Now.”

The answer comes back too fast, breathless with movement and jungle noise. “I’m on my way.”

Luke cuts the channel and keeps his hand there for a moment longer, thumb resting on the toggle. He looks at you, then at Tionne, then at the open seal. “That should have been enough.”

A distant thump rolls up through the stone under your feet. Dust skates off the edge of the circular floor. The seal is still open. The lower Massassi levels answer with a second удар—harder, closer—and the temple gives a deep groan like a hull taking strain.

Tionne’s head turns toward the doorway. “That is not rain.”

Luke is already moving. “Stay here.”

He takes two steps, stops, and looks back at you instead of giving the order twice. His face has gone still in a way you have not seen from him before. “If Kira comes in alone, bring her to the center. If she does not—”

The third удар cuts him off. Not below. Sideways. Something heavy hits stone in the corridor outside the meditation level, and the nearest brazier shivers in its bracket. The smell that follows is hot metal and old dust.

Luke’s hand goes to the lightsaber at his belt, but he does not draw it.

You have a clean line to the seal, a clear corridor, and the feeling that the temple just changed from old to fragile.
choices: Hold your ground at the seal and keep your voice level when Kira comes in. If Luke is about to tell the truth, you make sure she hears it from both of you.
Go to the doorway and listen for where that second удар came from. If something is in the lower Massassi levels, you want the shape of it before anyone runs blind.
Tell Luke to get the other students clear of the meditation level and mean it. If this is becoming a problem, you help him protect the room before you chase answers.

Push the thought of Kira aside for one breath and listen into the stone itself. If the dark-side vergence beneath the temple is stirring, you want to know whether it is warning you or calling something up.

turns.action: Hold your ground at the seal and keep your voice level when Kira comes in. If Luke is about to tell the truth, you make sure she hears it from both of you.
turns.narration:
You hold your ground at the seal, and Luke takes the step he started toward the comm panel and stops. He turns his head toward the corridor instead of the door, one hand still hovering near his belt. The brazier beside him rattles once more, then settles with a thin click.

Kira comes in at a run from the corridor, breathing hard, one sleeve dark with dust and the other hand wrapped around the edge of the doorframe like she needs it to keep the room still. She sees Luke’s face, then yours, and the motion goes out of her all at once. She goes very still. That is worse than panic.

“What happened?” she asks, too fast to be calm.

Luke answers first. “Something hit the corridor wall. Stay back.”

Kira’s eyes flick past him toward the sound, then back to you. “That doesn’t sound like something,” she says, and the attempt at humor lands thin. Her fingers tighten on the frame until the knuckles pale.

Luke looks at the seal, then at Kira. He does not soften it. “You’ve been going below.”

The color drains from her face so quickly you see it under the temple’s warm light. She swallows once. “I was going to tell you.”

“You were going to go alone,” you say.

That lands harder. Her mouth opens, shuts, and she looks at the floor stones between you, as if they might offer a cleaner answer.

Luke folds his arms. “The lower Massassi levels are not a place for half-truths.”

Kira lets out a breath through her nose, sharp and angry. “Then start with the whole truth.”

Luke holds that for a beat. When he speaks, his voice is flat and exact. “There is a dark-side vergence beneath the Great Temple. It is old. It is strong enough to call to someone who is sensitive to it. I kept you away because I thought waiting was safer than sending you there unprepared.”

Kira stares at him. The anger does not leave. It changes shape, turns hard around the edges. “You thought I wouldn’t notice you leaving pieces out.”

“No,” Luke says. “I thought I could give you the pieces in order.”

That almost draws a laugh from you, but the sound never makes it out. Kira hears it anyway in your face. Her eyes cut to you, then back to Luke. “So what now?”

Luke glances once at the corridor, then back to both of you. “Now we do this together. No one goes below alone.”

Kira’s hand drops from the doorframe. Dust leaves a gray print across her palm. She looks like she wants to argue, and like she already knows the argument will fail.
choices: Tell Kira you are not letting her meet the lower Massassi levels by herself, and keep your voice gentle enough that it sounds like loyalty, not a warning.
Ask Luke, in front of Kira, what he knows about the dark-side vergence beneath the Great Temple that he still has not said out loud
Turn to Kira and say plainly that whatever is waiting below has already started pulling on her, so you need her honest before you all go anywhere
Stay with the feeling in your chest for one more breath, then decide whether you trust Luke’s order more than Kira’s curiosity.
